question: After the conflict is resolved, should maintainers accept the focused runner/Codex regression proof for this lane-release fix, or require live Codex app-server or WhatsApp wedge proof before merge?
rationale: The code path is a bug fix, but it deliberately releases same-session ownership while Codex cleanup can still be unsettled and the PR carries human-review/proof-decision signals.

options.title: Accept focused proof after conflict repair
options.body: Resolve the branch conflict, rerun required checks on the exact head, and accept the focused regression as sufficient for the runner-owned lane-release contract.

options.title: Require live wedge proof
options.body: Pause merge until a live or Crabbox Codex app-server wedge demonstrates that late cleanup does not corrupt session state or message delivery.

options.title: Pause or replace
options.body: Close or replace this branch if resolving the current-main conflict would require broad churn beyond the narrow lane-release fix.

recommendation.title: Accept focused proof after conflict repair
recommendation.body: Resolve the branch conflict, rerun required checks on the exact head, and accept the focused regression as sufficient for the runner-owned lane-release contract.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is tied to the current runner lines, the adjacent native lane-release merge, and the source PR automerge path.
